title: Howl's Moving Castle (film) — Survival, Reproduction, Illusion #Shorts
description:
The psychology underneath Howl's Moving Castle (film) is simpler and older than the story on top. Howl's Moving Castle is a 2004 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, based on Diana Wynne Jones' 1986 novel. The film was produced by Toshio Suzuki, animated by Studio Ghibli, and distributed by Toho.

Take away the meaning and Howl's Moving Castle (film) still functions — that is the disturbing part. Elizabeth Parsons stated that the film disrupts the stereotype of "aged unattractiveness," when the artificially aged Sophie manages to rescue two attractive men (who come to love her) and to unintentionally end the war in her country. Sophie's actions are those usually associated with grandmothers, such as being kind and nurturing to those around her, and engaging in housework; however, these actions are depicted as being powerful and heroic.
